production.note: US model years. Quote (Motor Authority, Stephen Edelstein, 4 October 2021): "due to start sales in the U.S. in spring 2022 as a 2023 model". Still on sale: Lotus's US site lists the Emira V6 SE: "The Emira V6 SE features a supercharged 3.5-litre V6 engine, paired with the coveted 6-speed manual gearbox" (lotus-us-emira-page).

body.note: 'an all-new mid-engine premium sports car'; fixed-roof two-seater, no open version.

configuration.note: 'Supercharged 3.5-litre 400hp V6' (Toyota 2GR-FE). The four-cylinder Emira is a separate variant.

drivetrain.note: The Drive's spec box: "3.5-liter supercharged V6 | 6-speed manual | rear-wheel drive"

transmission.note: Lotus: 'six-speed manual transmission as standard, optional six-speed auto with paddleshift'. Carscoops on the US car: "a standard six-speed manual ... but customers can opt for a six-speed automatic transmission for an additional $2,150" (carscoops-emira-us-price). The automatic is a torque-converter gearbox.

powerHp.note: Quote (Lotus release): "Developing 400hp, it's mated to a six-speed manual gearbox with a visible gearchange mechanism and hydraulic power-assisted steering." For the US car, Carscoops (Michael Gauthier, 1 October 2021): "This enables it to produce 400 hp (298 kW / 405 PS) and up to 317 lb-ft" (carscoops-emira-us-price); Motor Authority: "in the Emira it generates a peak 400 hp" (motorauthority-emira-2023). 298 kW x 1.34102 = 400 hp, so Lotus's figure is horsepower, used as published; Lotus does not call it an SAE rating, so powerStandard is Other. The Drive's spec box prints "Horsepower: 395" (thedrive-emira-2023); see discrepancies. Car and Driver's road-test panel for the 2024 First Edition prints the same rating: "Power: 400 hp @ 6800 rpm" (cd-emira-first-edition-2024), so 400 hp holds for the reference year 2024.

weightLb.note: Weight-order step 2: Car and Driver road-test curb weight (owner decision, 9 October 2026, docs/DATA_GUIDE.md); a measured weight of C/D's test car. Car and Driver road-test panel '2024 Lotus Emira First Edition' (owner copy), quote: "Curb Weight: 3279 lb". The First Edition tested is the V6: "Supercharged DOHC 24-valve V-6, aluminum block and heads, port injection", "Displacement: 211 in3, 3456 cm3", "Power: 400 hp @ 6800 rpm", "TRANSMISSION" / "6-speed manual" (the standard transmission), "mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive, 2-passenger, 2-door coupe", "Base/As Tested: $107,500/$107,500", "Options: none". This replaces the earlier provisional 3,097 lb (The Drive, Motor Authority), Lotus's pre-production target for the car 'in its lightest form' (step 3), which was not stated to be the V6 (CarExpert: 'Lotus is targeting a kerb weight of 1405kg in the car's lightest form', carexpert-emira-2021); see discrepancies. Reference year 2024: the panel describes a 2024 car, and no qualifying weight exists for 2023 (the 2023 figure was only a target).

discrepancies.reason: Configuration, method and market: 3,097 lb was Lotus's pre-production target for the lightest car; 1,457 kg is Evo's claimed kerb weight for a UK car in a 2026 review; Car and Driver's 3,279 lb is the measured curb weight of a US 2024 V6 First Edition with the manual and no options.
discrepancies.resolution: Owner decision, 9 October 2026: the Car and Driver road-test curb weight is used (docs/DATA_GUIDE.md, Weight step 2). 3,279 lb used, and the reference year moved to 2024 (the panel's year); the earlier 3,097 lb (lightweight-options target) was the provisional figure.

provisionalNote: Only the first US model year is provisional: Motor Authority says the car came 'as a 2023 model', while Kelley Blue Book lists the Emira only from 2024. A Lotus Cars USA release or price list naming the first US model year would settle it. Weight (3,279 lb, Car and Driver road-test curb weight of the 2024 V6 First Edition, manual) and power (400 hp, Lotus, confirmed by the same panel) are no longer provisional; the reference year is 2024, the panel's year.
